To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bilateral cochlear implants provide significant benefit for localization and speech intelligiblity, that localization emerges before localization and speech intelligbility, and that speech intelligibility and localization are correlated.

(a) sound localization and speech intelligiblity in noise are both better when listening with two ears than with one ear; (b) sound localization emerges before sound localization in the hemifield; (c) speech intelligibility is better with bilateral than unilateral stimulation; (d) the benefit of bilateral hearing for speech intelligibility increases with time, in contrast to the sound localization ability; and (e) speech intelligibility in noise is better when the target speech is presented from a different location

(a) bilateral cochlear implant users are able to localize sounds to the right versus the left, (b) bilateral cochlear implants improve speech intelligibility, and (c) the improvement in speech intelligibility is greater for spatially separated than colocated speech and noise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ability of listeners with cochlear implants to use the spatial cues in sound to understand speech in a complex listening environment.
the development of spatial hearing skills, including sound localization, lateralization, and speech segregation, in a group of adult cochlear implant users.
the development of spatial hearing and speech intelligibility with bilateral cochlear implant use in adults who have been deafened postlingually.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

bilateral hearing through cochleair implantation provides the opportunity for the development of directional hearing, and that this ability is associated with improved speech intelligibility in a complex auditory scene.
bilateral hearing through cochleaimplants provides a significant benefit to spatial hearing and speech intelligibility.
bilateral cochlear implantation provides a significant benefit for sound localization and speech intelligibilty in postlingually-deafened adults.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ability to localize sounds is an important factor in speech perception, particularly in the presence of competing noise.
the benefits of bilateral cochlear implants are not only related to the ability to hear speech, but also the ability to locate sound sources and to segregate speech from competing noise.
the ability to use spatial cues to segregate target speech from interfering noise is a skill that emerges in the early months of bilateral cochlear implantation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bilateral hearing with cochlear implants is a complex process that is not fully mature at 6 mo of use.

the emergence of directional hearing in postlingually-deafened adults is a gradual process, and that it is important to continue to assess and improve the ability to hear in a complex acoustic environment.
bilateral hearing is a powerful tool for speech understanding in noise, and that this benefit increases over time as patients learn to use the spatial cues provided by the two implants.
